Lukas / team —

We started seeing a sustained surge in cold-start latency on our private cluster (VPC) this morning around 04:30 local. P95 for text-generation endpoints jumped from ~1.2s to 5.6s and we're seeing intermittent 502s during nightly batch windows. Error rate is hovering ~7% for the last 3 hours.

Attached: synergia_diagnostics_20280621.zip (logs + traces), sample 502s in error_sample_502s.log.

What we've tried so far: a) reduced batch window (no change), b) restarted a small pool of worker nodes (partial improvement for a few minutes), c) rolled fallback to a smaller model variant (reduced throughput but still p95 elevated).

This is impacting production inference for two clinical pipelines (non-blocking for patient safety but causing SLA misses). We need a triage and a clear timeline for stabilization — and an exec sync if this will take more than 4 hours.

Can you confirm next steps and an ETA? Also adding Carlos (CTO) for visibility.

Thanks,
Jane Park

Adding context from account side: Synergia has a night-batch workload that issues many short-lived cold-start requests (avg seq_len 200, high concurrency between 03:30-06:00). Historically we've used aggressive KV cache persistence to mitigate that pattern.

Suggested customer-facing mitigations (short-term):
- Enable persistent KV cache for the affected pool (saves warmup time).
- Reduce max_seq to 512 as Lukas suggested.
- Roll to the fallback model variant with reduced memory footprint for the busiest routes to remove memory pressure on the node.

If we cannot bring the error rate below 1% in the next 2 hours, request an exec sync with Synergia (Carlos + Head of Ops) to propose a short maintenance window and temporary credits for SLA exposure.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Platform Engineering <platform-eng@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jane Park <jane.park@synergiahealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-21 15:20 -0700
Subject: Re: kernel/decoder suspicion — suggested mitigations and canary steps

We're seeing signs that the decoder kernel schedule is getting starved under transient warmup spikes; "failed to claim execution slot" + kernel launch timeout points to queue saturation at the CUDA stream level. Immediate engine-level mitigations to try (low-risk canary):

1) Reduce per-request max_seq to 512 centrally: limits worst-case kernel cycles.
2) Set ENV REDWOOD_CUDA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL=1 for affected pool to favor persistent kernel reuse (reduces launch overhead).
3) Temporarily lower decode concurrency to 4 threads per node and increase worker count by +2 nodes to preserve throughput.
4) Increase KV cache persistence TTL from 30s to 10m to reduce cold-starts.

Commands (canary):
- redwoodctl pool update --id pool-sy-01 --env REDWOOD_CUDA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL=1
- redwoodctl model config set --model sy-model-a --max_seq 512
- redwoodctl pool scale --id pool-sy-01 --add-workers 2

I'll prepare a canary patch and monitor p95/error-rate for 30m. If no improvement, we'll pull a lightweight kernel recompile and stage to canary nodes (patch window ~45m).

— Markus
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
